label: JZ Mock C · Paper 2 · Question 10
knowledgePattern: Compare how quickly truth checks can distinguish answer patterns
solution:
A single check can identify an option if its true or false outcome occurs for only one option. In Set I, statement 3 occurs only in B. In Set II, a true result for any one statement identifies its own option. In Set III, statement 1 occurs only in A, and statement 5 only in D. Thus these sets each allow identification after just one lucky check.

In Set IV, each statement occurs in two options and fails in three. Neither outcome of any one check identifies a unique option, so at least two checks are always needed.

If statements 1 and 2 both turn out true, only A in Set IV contains both, so two checks can be sufficient. Therefore Set IV has the greatest best-case minimum, namely two. Answer D.

hints.title: Think about what one check tells you
hints.body: Choose a statement number. In each set, mark which answer options say it is true and which say it is false.
hints.recap: An outcome identifies the answer only if exactly one option remains possible.
hints.pitfall: A check can return false as well as true.
hints.pause: Look for a statement whose true or false outcome leaves a single option.

recall.reminder: Split into all possible outcomes of the check, including true and false.

hints.title: Use the best-case meaning of luck
hints.body: You need the fewest checks that could identify an answer if the results go your way. If no single check works, try two statement checks together.
hints.recap: A least possible number needs both a reason fewer cannot work and an example that achieves it.
hints.pitfall: This asks what a lucky student could do, not how many checks always guarantee success.
hints.pause: Find this minimum for each set and choose the greatest of those minima.

recall.reminder: A least possible number needs both a reason fewer cannot work and an example that achieves it.
